play.data.habits: Your playing habits, only as summary numbers (for example where your clicks tend to land, or how much the still cursor shakes): to adapt the setup to the way you play. In a file on this PC (habits.json); deleted with "Forget my habits".
play.rule.msg.area_shift: Move the area a little towards where you already aim.
play.rule.msg.area_size: Fit the area size to your jumps.
play.rule.msg.area_rotate: Turn the area slightly, the way your wrist turns.
play.rule.msg.smoothing_lighter: Lighter smoothing, so the cursor arrives on time.
play.rule.msg.smoothing_remove: Less smoothing, so the cursor responds sooner.
play.rule.msg.smoothing_add_light: Very light smoothing, only for the shake while the pen is still.
play.rule.msg.flag_emi: This looks like interference: nothing changes this time.
play.rule.msg.wait: Give your hand time: nothing changes this time.
play.rule.why.emi: The cursor made {n} impossible jumps during the play. That is not your hand: it is usually interference (a cable, a charger or the monitor very close to the tablet). An experienced player would not touch the setup after a play like this, so nothing changes this time.
play.rule.why.wait_area: You changed the area recently. An experienced player would let the hand get used to it for a few days before tuning again (about {days} days to go); meanwhile the coach leaves it alone. You can still play, and move it by hand if you prefer.
play.rule.why.wait_smoothing: You recently started playing with much less smoothing. Getting used to it takes from a few days to a couple of weeks (about {days} days to go); an experienced player would wait before touching the area, so the coach leaves it alone for now.
play.rule.why.stacked: You have {a} and {b} on at the same time. An experienced player would use a single smoothing filter: two together add up their delay. {name} is switched off (its values are kept in case you want it back).
play.rule.why.lighter: On fast jumps the cursor arrives a little late, and on slow ones it does not: that comes from the smoothing, not from the area. An experienced player would take {name} one level down before touching the area.
play.rule.why.off: On fast jumps the cursor arrives a little late, and on slow ones it does not: that comes from the smoothing, not from the area. An experienced player would try without {name} before touching the area (its values are kept).
play.rule.why.hardware: On fast jumps the cursor arrives somewhat late although no smoothing is on; some tablets smooth internally. That is an advanced setting, so the coach does not touch it.
play.rule.why.shift: Over {plays} plays your clicks tend to land a little to the same side. An experienced player would move the area {mm} mm towards {towards}: the movement you already make then ends right on the centre of the circle.
play.rule.why.clamp: Sometimes the pen leaves the area on that side right when you go for a circle. An experienced player would move the area {mm} mm towards {towards} so your hand has room there.
play.rule.why.rotate_cw: Over {plays} plays your jumps come out slightly turned, always clockwise; that is very common because of how the wrist rests. An experienced player would turn the area {deg}° the same way, so your natural movement goes straight.
play.rule.why.rotate_ccw: Over {plays} plays your jumps come out slightly turned, always counter-clockwise; that is very common because of how the wrist rests. An experienced player would turn the area {deg}° the same way, so your natural movement goes straight.
play.rule.why.axis: Over {plays} plays you do not reach the same horizontally as vertically. An experienced player would make the area {pct} % {way}, leaving the other axis alone; the proportion would be {ratio}.
play.rule.why.size_up: Over {plays} plays you go a little past the circle, more the longer the jump. An experienced player would make the area {pct} % bigger: the same hand movement then covers a little less screen and lands inside.
play.rule.why.size_down: Over {plays} plays you stop a little short on jumps, more the longer they are. An experienced player would make the area {pct} % smaller: the same movement then reaches the circle.
play.rule.why.tremor: With the pen still, the cursor shakes quite a bit. An experienced player would make the area {pct} % bigger: the same shake then shows less on the screen.
play.rule.why.hover: The cursor shakes mostly during breaks, or the tablet loses the pen now and then: that usually happens when the pen is higher than the tablet reads well. Smoothing does not help with that, so none is added.
play.rule.why.add_light: With the pen still the cursor shakes a little, but your jumps are fine. An experienced player would try very light smoothing ({name}): it calms the shake and adds almost no delay.
play.rule.why.late: You tend to tap about {ms} ms late. That is set with osu!'s global offset (or by watching the hit error bar), not with the area.
play.rule.why.early_offset: You tend to tap about {ms} ms early. That is set with osu!'s global offset (or by watching the hit error bar), not with the area.
play.rule.why.early_tap: You tap before reaching the circle, so some clicks land just before it. That is a matter of rhythm, not of the area, so the area does not change for it.
play.rule.why.edge_stop: You tend to brake as you enter the circle, near its edge, whatever the jump. That is a way of playing: the area is not changed for it.
play.rule.why.keep: For now nothing in the way you play asks for a clear change: the best is to keep the setup as it is.
play.rule.acc.shift: That is why the area moves {mm} mm towards {towards}.
play.rule.acc.rotate_cw: That is why the area turns {deg}° clockwise.
play.rule.acc.rotate_ccw: That is why the area turns {deg}° counter-clockwise.
play.rule.acc.axis: That is why the area becomes {pct} % {way}.
play.rule.acc.size_up: That is why the area grows {pct} %.
play.rule.acc.size_down: That is why the area shrinks {pct} %.
play.rule.acc.lighter: That is why {name} goes one level lighter.
play.rule.acc.off: That is why the coach tries without {name}.
play.rule.acc.stacked: That is why only one smoothing filter stays on.
play.rule.acc.add_light: That is why the coach tries {name}, very light.
play.rule.acc.emi: While there is interference, the coach tunes nothing.
play.rule.acc.wait_area: That is why the area stays as it is these days.
play.rule.acc.wait_smoothing: That is why the area stays as it is these days.
play.rule.acc.keep: The setup does not change for this.
play.rule.acc.offset: This belongs in osu!'s offset; the area does not change.
play.rule.acc.timing: It is a matter of rhythm: the area does not change for it.
play.rule.acc.edge_stop: It is your way of playing: the area does not change for it.
play.rule.acc.hover: Smoothing does not help here, so none is added.
play.rule.acc.later: This can be adapted too, in another round (one change at a time).
play.rule.acc.unsure: Not sure yet: more plays are needed.
play.rule.acc.tap: That works well: the setup does not change for it.
play.rule.acc.drift: The setup does not change for this; if it happens often, the tablet may be sliding a little on the desk.
play.rule.acc.fatigue: That is normal on long maps; the setup does not change for it.
play.style.title: Your playing style
play.style.acted_title: What the setup does for you
play.style.fine_title: Seen, but nothing needs to change
play.style.privacy: This stays on this PC (habits.json), only as summary numbers: no positions, maps or scores.
play.style.forget_confirm: Delete everything the coach learned about the way you play? It will start getting to know you again.
play.style.forgotten: Done: the coach forgot your habits and will start from scratch.
play.style.forget_failed: The habits file could not be deleted; try again in a moment.
play.style.headline.acted: The coach fits your setup to the way you play; you do not have to change anything.
play.style.headline.learning: The coach is still getting to know the way you play: one or two more plays will tell it more.
play.style.headline.fits: The way you play fits your current setup: nothing needs to change for it.
play.style.aim_bias: Your clicks land a little towards {towards} of the circle centres.
play.style.size_over: On jumps you tend to go a little past the circle, more the longer they are.
play.style.size_short: You tend to stop a little short on jumps, more the longer they are.
play.style.aspect_x: Horizontally you reach a bit further than vertically.
play.style.aspect_y: Vertically you reach a bit further than horizontally.
play.style.rotation_cw: Your jumps come out slightly turned clockwise (very common because of how the wrist rests).
play.style.rotation_ccw: Your jumps come out slightly turned counter-clockwise (very common because of how the wrist rests).
play.style.edge_stop: You tend to brake as you enter the circle, near its edge.
play.style.edge_past: You tend to end the jump a little past the centre, long or short.
play.style.trail: On very fast jumps the cursor arrives a touch late.
play.style.tap_early: You tap slightly before reaching the circle (about {ms} ms).
play.style.tap_after: You reach the circle first and then tap (about {ms} ms later).
play.style.timing_late: You tend to tap about {ms} ms late.
play.style.timing_early: You tend to tap about {ms} ms early.
play.style.key_gap: With {late} you tap about {ms} ms later than with {early}.
play.style.jitter: With the pen still, the cursor shakes a little more than usual.
play.style.steady: With the pen still, the cursor is very steady.
play.style.hover: The cursor shakes more during breaks than while you play.
play.style.pen_lift: Sometimes the tablet stops seeing the pen right when a circle comes.
play.style.drift: Over the map, your clicks slowly move towards {towards}.
play.style.fatigue: Towards the end of long maps, the aim spreads out a little.
play.style.spikes: The cursor made an impossible jump (a teleport): that is not your hand.
play.style.clamp: Sometimes the pen leaves the area on the side of {towards}.
play.style.long_short: You tend to stop a little short on long jumps towards {towards}.
play.style.long_over: You tend to go a little past on long jumps towards {towards}.
play.style.zone_short: {place}: there you stop a little short (a small zone).
play.style.zone_over: {place}: there you go a little past (a small zone).
play.style.zone_off: {place}: there your clicks drift a little (a small zone).
play.style.warn.failed: Your habits could not be measured in this play.
play.style.warn.untrusted: This play did not line up well with the map, so it does not count for your habits.
play.style.warn.relax: With Relax or Autopilot the clicks or the aim are not yours: this play does not count for your habits.
play.style.warn.mods_mismatch: The replay's mods do not match what the coach saw; this play's habits are less reliable.
